label: Finite recombination plus prefix closure permits every complete suffix
paraphrase: For each fixed all-true observed prefix and supplied selector of complete Boolean histories: nonempty one-step continuation freedom implies the existence of extensions for every prescribed finite pattern. Adding the separate prefix-closure principle implies that every complete infinite suffix is admitted. An eventually constant, populated selector has one-step and finite freedom but neither closure nor unrestricted infinite histories; a stable selector is closed but lacks finite freedom; unrestricted and empty selectors witness the positive and nonemptiness controls. No claim derives either premise from unexplained actuality or assigns modal/physical status to these trace histories.
